title: PCL staleness age never shown — badge has no timestamp
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx — stale badge render block; data.lastSyncedAt available in API response

Root Cause: When pclStatus === 'stale', a yellow badge is shown but no age calculation is performed. The lastSyncedAt field is already available in the API response and is used for the "Synced {date}" text in the header. However, no daysAgo or hoursAgo value is computed and displayed alongside the badge.

Claude Fix Prompt: In FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx, compute staleness age where lastSyncedAt is available:
```js
const syncAge = data?.lastSyncedAt
  ? Math.floor((Date.now() - new Date(data.lastSyncedAt).getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24))
  : null;
```
Update the stale badge to: <Badge colorScheme="orange">Data may be stale ({syncAge !== null ? `${syncAge}d ago` : 'unknown'})</Badge>. Add a tooltip: "Coverage data is from a snapshot. Trigger a sync to refresh."
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — syncAge computed (FrameworkComplianceMap lines 795–804); badge shows `· Nd ago`

title: `coveragePercent` shows 0% for all active frameworks before first PCL sync
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/app/(private)/grc-framework/page.jsx — stats cards; vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworksManager.jsx — framework tile progress bar

Root Cause: For new projects that have never triggered a PCL sync, frameworkScores[] in the PCL is empty. The page.jsx merges PCL scores into frameworks using scoreMap.get(String(fw.frameworkId)) — when this returns undefined, coveragePercent defaults to 0. The stats card shows "0% Overall Compliance" and all framework tiles show a 0% progress bar with no explanation that PCL has not been run.

Claude Fix Prompt:
1. In page.jsx, after building merged, check if pclData is null or pclData.frameworkScores is empty. If so, set a pclNotSynced flag.
2. If pclNotSynced, show an <Alert status="info"> above the stats: "No compliance snapshot exists for this project yet. Trigger a PCL sync from any active framework's compliance map to populate coverage data."
3. In FrameworksManager.jsx, when fw.coveragePercent === 0 AND the framework is active, show "Not yet synced" instead of a 0% progress bar, conditioned on whether the parent passed a pclNotSynced prop.
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — pclNotSynced flag (page.jsx line 39); info Alert (lines 162–169); "not synced yet" text (FrameworksManager line 324)

title: No deactivation audit trail — archivedBy/archivedAt not stored
description:
Files: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/compliance-frameworks/client-frameworks.controller.js — archiveByFrameworkId(); vibrantix-backend/src/modules/compliance-frameworks/models/client-framework.model.js

Root Cause: archiveByFrameworkId() sets status: 'archived' on the ClientFramework document but does not set archivedBy (the userId from the authenticated request) or archivedAt (timestamp). The ClientFramework model has detachedAt and revokedAt fields but no archivedAt or archivedByUserId fields. There is no audit log entry created. ISO 27001 Clause 9.3 requires that management review inputs include framework scope changes.

Claude Fix Prompt:
1. In client-framework.model.js, add: archivedAt: { type: Date, default: null } and archivedBy: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'ClientUser', default: null }.
2. In archiveByFrameworkId(): await ClientFramework.findOneAndUpdate({ projectId, frameworkId }, { status: 'archived', archivedAt: new Date(), archivedBy: req.userId }).
3. In the listByProject response, include archivedAt and archivedByName (populated) so the UI can show "Deactivated by {name} on {date}" in the inactive framework tile.
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — archivedAt+archivedBy in schema (model lines 17–18); set in archiveByFrameworkId (controller lines 155–156) and archiveFromProject (lines 138–139)

title: Domain accordion resets scroll position on every filter change
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx — <Accordion defaultIndex={[0]}> and filteredDomains re-render trigger

Root Cause: The Accordion component uses defaultIndex={[0]} and filteredDomains.map(...) as children. When any filter changes, filteredDomains recomputes from useMemo, causing the accordion to re-render. Because DomainAccordionItem components are keyed by dg.domain, domains that remain visible persist state — but the scroll position of the page is not preserved. For frameworks with 11+ domains (ISO 27001), users scrolled to domain 8 are teleported to the top when typing a search query.

Claude Fix Prompt:
1. Add useRef to save the scroll position before filter updates: const scrollRef = useRef(0).
2. In the filter change handlers (setSearch, setStatusFilter, etc.), save scrollRef.current = window.scrollY before the state update.
3. Use a useEffect on filteredDomains to restore: useEffect(() => { window.scrollTo(0, scrollRef.current); }, [filteredDomains]).
4. Alternatively, keep the accordion in allowMultiple mode and persist open domain indices in a useState([0]) that is NOT reset on filter changes.
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — scrollYRef = useRef(0) (line 601); useEffect restores on filteredDomains change (lines 719–723)

title: FrameworksManager Show More pagination resets after any toggle action
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworksManager.jsx — activeVisible / inactiveVisible state; useEffect that re-initialises from frameworks prop

Root Cause: When the frameworks prop changes (after a toggle triggers onRefresh), the useEffect that calls setActiveFrameworks(...) and setInactiveFrameworks(...) runs and splits the updated list. However, activeVisible and inactiveVisible are not reset in this effect — but the re-render caused by setActiveFrameworks also doesn't preserve the activeVisible value because it's managed separately. In practice any prop change causes a reconciliation that renders all visible=10 items.

Claude Fix Prompt: In FrameworksManager.jsx, store activeVisible and inactiveVisible in useRef instead of useState so they do not trigger re-renders and are not affected by framework prop updates. Access via activeVisibleRef.current when slicing for render. Only update refs (not state) on "Show More" click. The visible count persists across prop-driven re-renders because refs are not reset by React's reconciliation.
fixEvidence: Run #1 analysis: pagination resets only on filter changes (correct UX); toggle actions use local state and do NOT reset visible counters — root cause was inaccurate

title: Coverage percent triple-rounded across PCL → backend → frontend
description:
Files: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/compliance-frameworks/project-compliance-lookup.controller.js — frameworkScores[].coveragePercent; vibrantix-client-panel/src/app/(private)/grc-framework/page.jsx — overallCompliance computation; vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx — stats card stat prop

Root Cause: coveragePercent is computed with Math.round() in the PCL controller. Then page.jsx averages framework.coveragePercent values and calls Math.round() again for the overall stats card. Then FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx calls Math.round(fw?.coveragePercent ?? 0) a third time for the compliance map stats strip. Each rounding can introduce ±0.5% error; compounded over multiple frameworks with partial controls, the displayed value can differ from the true computed value by 1–2%.

Claude Fix Prompt:
1. Store coveragePercent as a float (2 decimal places) in the PCL — remove Math.round() from the PCL controller.
2. Apply Math.round() only at the final display layer in the React components.
3. In FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx StatsCard, the stat prop already calls Math.round() — no change needed there.
4. In page.jsx, compute overallCompliance from raw float values: Math.round(scoredFrameworks.reduce(...) / scoredFrameworks.length) — this is the single rounding point for the overview stats.
fixEvidence: Run #2 verified — PCL sync service (out-of-scope) still stores pre-rounded integers; frontend applies single Math.round; harmless until PCL service updated

title: Polling during sync fetches full compliance-map payload instead of lightweight /pcl/status
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/grc/FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx — handleSync() lines 655–679

Root Cause: The polling loop in handleSync() calls complianceService.getFrameworkComplianceMap(projectId, frameworkId) on every poll tick. This endpoint fetches all controls for the framework, then enriches each one by joining PCL coverage data, evidence docs, policy docs, vendor rows, cloud rows, and integration rows. For ISO 27001 (93 controls), this can return 200–400 KB of JSON per poll. Multiplied by up to 10 poll attempts, the user receives up to 4 MB of redundant data while just waiting for a status change. The lightweight GET /projects/:projectId/pcl/status endpoint already exists and returns only ~200 bytes per response.

Claude Fix Prompt: In FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx handleSync(), split the polling into two phases:
1. Poll using complianceService.getPCLStatus(projectId) (add this to complianceService.js as async getPCLStatus(projectId) { return await get('/compliance-frameworks/projects/' + projectId + '/pcl/status'); }) every 3 seconds until status leaves 'computing'.
2. Only when status is confirmed as 'ready' or 'stale', call loadData() once to refresh the full compliance map.
This reduces network traffic by ~99% during polling and dramatically lowers server load for large frameworks.
fixEvidence: Run #2 fix — added `getPCLStatus()` to complianceService.js; handleSync() now polls lightweight endpoint; triggers `loadData()` once on completion

title: `hasAssets` calculation omits cloud and integrations arrays — controls with only cloud/integration coverage appear as `no_assets`
description:
Files: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/compliance-frameworks/project-compliance-lookup.controller.js — line 387

Root Cause: The hasAssets boolean on each enriched control is computed as:
```js
hasAssets: evidence.length + policies.length + vendors.length + certifications.length > 0
```
The cloud and integrations arrays are excluded from this sum. A control that has only cloud posture checks (e.g., AWS CIS benchmarks mapped to ISO 27001 A.8.x) or only external integration verdicts will have hasAssets: false despite having coverage-contributing data. The frontend no_assets filter includes these controls, and the status-filter guard (GRC-010) correctly excludes no_assets + covered combinations — but the false negative in hasAssets means: (a) controls with cloud/integration coverage show No assets chip in the control row, and (b) selecting No Assets filter hides controls that actually have assets, misrepresenting the compliance posture.

Claude Fix Prompt: In project-compliance-lookup.controller.js, update line 387:
```js
hasAssets: evidence.length + policies.length + vendors.length + certifications.length + cloud.length + integrationsOut.length > 0,
```
This ensures cloud checks and integration verdicts are counted as assets, consistent with how coverageScore is computed (which does include cloud and integration dimension scores).
fixEvidence: Run #2 fix — pcl controller hasAssets now includes `+ cloud.length + integrationsOut.length`
